synthesis.body: When a lint extracts file paths from prose (e.g. the spec-metadata lint's invariant (iii) flagging dangling code references in specs), false positives are the dominant risk. Three rules keep it precise: (1) only treat a token as a path if it's a FULL repo-relative path — contains '/', rooted at a known top-level dir (packages/ tools/ packs/ docs/ apps/ .github/) or an explicit ../ / ./ relative link, ending in a recognised extension after stripping a :line/#anchor locator; bare basenames (install.py) can't be located and must be skipped. (2) Exclude non-literal shorthands: placeholders (<...>), globs (*), AND brace-expansion ({a,b}.py) — all denote not-a-single-path. (3) In the self-test, PAIR each exclusion case with a shape-matched ACCEPTING control that DOES fire (e.g. glob `tools/lint-*.py` rejected + `tools/lint-missing.py` warns), so a no-op extractor that matches nothing fails the suite instead of passing every reject vacuously. Keep such a check WARN-ONLY until the corpus warn rate is measured — promoting to hard requires the existing backlog of true positives (often on Frozen specs you can't edit) to be cleaned first. Dogfooding catch: the lint will flag its OWN spec's illustrative example paths — use real resolvable paths (e.g. the lint's own path under packs/core/.apm/skills/work-loop/scripts/) as examples, not tools/x.py.

title: Prose-path-extraction lints: gate on full rooted paths, exclude placeholder/glob/brace shorthand, pair each exclusion test with an accepting control
